topic: Why Bitcoin price does not rise
question: Bitcoin got everything it spent fifteen years asking for. Why is it down 50%?
verdict: Because it got what it asked for. Institutional adoption was supposed to be the demand engine; instead it turned Bitcoin into an ordinary risk asset — correlated, liquidity-sensitive, and owned by people who sell when yields rise.

tension.expectation: Spot ETFs, a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, friendly regulators, corporate treasuries and retirement-account access were the entire bull case. All of them happened.
tension.reality: Bitcoin peaked at $126,198 on 2025-10-06 and trades near $60–65k in August 2026 — down roughly 50%.
tension.why_it_is_a_tension: The causal story everyone held (adoption → demand → price) ran forward exactly as predicted and produced the opposite outcome. That is not a disappointment, it is a broken model, and a broken model is the only thing worth 5 minutes.
tension.strength: high — the premise is checkable, widely believed, and demonstrably wrong

facts.claim: Bitcoin's all-time high was $126,198.07 on 6 October 2025
By 21 November 2025 it had fallen to $80,660 — a >30% drawdown in six weeks
In August 2026 Bitcoin trades near $60–65k, repeatedly capped at the $65,500–$67,000 region
facts.confidence: medium — price sources vary by a few thousand

facts.claim: That is a fall of nearly 50% from the October 2025 high
Trump signed the executive order establishing a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve on 6 March 2025
16 months later the White House concedes the long-term stockpile process is still being worked out, and agencies do not agree on how much BTC the US owns
facts.note: The flagship policy win is, in practice, unimplemented. Strong irony beat.

facts.claim: The GENIUS Act passed; regulators were replaced with crypto-friendly appointees; crypto access was expanded to retirement accounts
Long-term holders realised 3.67 million BTC in profit in the $100,000–$126,000 range — a larger distribution than any previous cycle
facts.confidence: medium — single aggregator, not verified against Glassnode/CryptoQuant primary

facts.claim: ETF inflows are not immediate spot demand: authorised participants often create and short ETF shares before buying the underlying bitcoin
facts.confidence: medium — mechanism reported by one analyst

facts.claim: Inflows have been positive but insufficient: holders who bought near these levels use recoveries to reduce positions, so ETF buying is absorbed by sellers rather than lifting price
Strategy's mNAV fell from 3.89x (Nov 2024) to below 1.0 — its market cap is worth less than the bitcoin it holds
MSTR fell ~70% between August 2025 and February 2026; the company reported a $12.4bn loss in Q4 2025
In June 2026 Strategy sold 32 BTC — a break from its 'never sell bitcoin' stance
facts.note: 32 BTC is trivially small in dollars. Its entire significance is symbolic — the policy broke, not the balance sheet.

facts.claim: Strategy built a cash reserve (from $1.44bn in Dec 2025) covering 2.5+ years of debt and dividends; Saylor claims it can cover $6bn of debt even at $8,000 BTC
facts.note: The steel-man. Include it — the forced-seller thesis is weaker than it looks.

facts.claim: Bitcoin's correlation with the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 sits in the 0.70–0.80 range in risk-on conditions
The 10-year Treasury yield approached a one-year high near 4.5% in March 2026; the 30-year hit 5% in April 2026
Analysts attribute price pressure to rising Treasury yields, a stronger dollar, tariffs, geopolitical tension and Fed policy — outweighing regulatory progress
Long-term holders added ~380,000 BTC (~$24.3bn, almost 2% of supply) over a 30-day window in mid-2026
facts.note: Corroborated in follow-up round 1 — but it was ONE COHORT, not the market. Mid-tier holders distributed more over the same window, which limits how much comfort it gives the steel-man.

facts.claim: Global M2 grew more than 12% over the last twelve months while Bitcoin fell roughly 12% — the liquidity relationship broke down through 2026
facts.note: Replaced f-liquidity in follow-up round 1. Stronger than what it replaces AND argues the same thesis: an asset that stopped responding to liquidity is being managed as a position.

facts.claim: Wallets holding over 1,000 BTC accumulated roughly 270,000 BTC in the 30 days to 23 April 2026, and again over a fortnight in late June/early July while price fell below $58,000
facts.period: 30 days to 2026-04-23, and a fortnight in late Jun/early Jul

facts.claim: Holders of 100-1,000 BTC distributed about 77,800 BTC, over a window the sources do not agree on
facts.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-12 by the gauntlet control migration. The original read "about 77,800 BTC over the same 60-day window - slightly more than the whale cohort absorbed": two arithmetic errors in one load-bearing sentence. The sibling f-whale-absorb dates its window at 30 days, not 60; and 77,800 is 29% of ~270,000, not "slightly more". It shipped into three scripts and fed c-scarcity-not-a-floor at leap:near. The cohort figure is kept because it is sourced; the comparison is gone because it was never true. This is the fact that forced facts[].unit/period and the arithmetic quality-bar row.

mechanisms.name: An ETF inflow is not a purchase
chain: A dollar enters a spot bitcoin ETF
THEREFORE the market reads it as new demand
BUT authorised participants can create and short ETF shares before buying the underlying
THEREFORE the buying is lagged and partly hedged
AND sellers at the same price level absorb what does arrive
THEREFORE inflow can be positive while price is flat
mechanisms.explains: Why 'record inflows' headlines coexist with a flat chart

mechanisms.name: The flywheel that only turns one way
chain: A treasury company's stock trades above the bitcoin it holds (mNAV > 1)
THEREFORE it can issue equity and buy more bitcoin, accretively
THEREFORE it becomes a permanent, price-insensitive buyer
BUT if the stock falls below the value of its holdings (mNAV < 1), issuing equity destroys shareholder value
AND the company's remaining tools are buybacks, dividends — and eventually selling bitcoin
THEREFORE the biggest structural buyer becomes, at the margin, a seller
mechanisms.explains: How the demand engine reversed direction

mechanisms.name: Adoption is correlation
chain: THEREFORE it enters portfolios governed by risk models
THEREFORE it is sized, hedged and rebalanced like any other risk asset
THEREFORE when real yields rise, it is sold alongside tech stocks
THEREFORE the adoption that was supposed to make it valuable is what made it ordinary
mechanisms.explains: THE THESIS — why the bull case was self-defeating
mechanisms.note: This is the video. Everything else is evidence for it.

reversals.obvious_reading: ETF inflows are positive, so demand is real and price should rise
reversals.why_wrong: An inflow is not a spot purchase, and what does get bought is absorbed by holders selling into it
reversals.escalation: The largest distribution of any cycle happened into exactly this demand

reversals.obvious_reading: Corporate treasuries are permanent buyers — they never sell
reversals.why_wrong: The buying was a function of the share price, not conviction. Below mNAV 1.0 the mechanism reverses.
reversals.escalation: In June 2026 the company that made 'never sell' a brand sold 32 coins

reversals.obvious_reading: Washington delivered — a reserve, an act, friendly regulators. That has to be bullish.
reversals.why_wrong: Regulatory permission is not demand, and the reserve was never actually built
reversals.escalation: 16 months on, agencies cannot agree how much bitcoin the government owns

reversals.why_wrong: It succeeded completely. That is the problem.
reversals.escalation: Bitcoin now moves on the 10-year Treasury yield — the single most boring number in finance
reversals.note: This is the final turn and the thesis. Save it.

steel_man.claim: The forced-seller story is weaker than it looks, and the accumulation story is real
steel_man.statement: Strategy holds 2.5+ years of debt and dividend coverage in cash and has not been forced to liquidate; 32 coins is a rounding error. And long-term holders added ~380,000 BTC in a single month this year — after the drawdown, not before. Nothing here says the asset is broken. Follow-up round 1 qualifies this: the accumulation was one cohort, and the tier directly below it sold slightly more over the same window.
steel_man.why_include: Without it the script is a bear case wearing an explainer's clothes. The honest position is 'the model changed', not 'it is going to zero'.

scale_conversions.felt: half the value, in ten months, while every piece of good news it ever wanted arrived
more coins sold into strength than in any previous cycle — the people who held longest sold most
the market went from paying $3.89 for every dollar of bitcoin the company held, to under a dollar
about $2 million — for a company holding billions. The number is meaningless; the sentence 'Strategy sold bitcoin' is not.
on most days, bitcoin is a tech stock with extra steps
when a government bond pays you to do nothing, an asset that yields nothing has to argue harder

analogy_candidates.analogy: A company that borrows against its own house to buy more houses. It works beautifully while house prices rise — and the moment the market values the company below the houses it owns, the only way to keep the lights on is to sell a house.
analogy_candidates.quality: strong — physical, familiar, carries the reversal

analogy_candidates.analogy: Money going into a fund is a promise to buy, not a purchase — like a restaurant taking a booking. A full reservation book and an empty dining room can be true at the same hour.
analogy_candidates.quality: medium — the shorting mechanism is not fully captured

analogy_candidates.analogy: Bitcoin spent fifteen years trying to get invited to the party, and the price of admission was becoming a guest like any other — subject to the same house rules.
analogy_candidates.quality: medium — abstract; consider dropping, the thesis may be stronger unadorned

candidate_questions: If the bull case came true, why is the price down?
Where did the ETF money actually go?
What happened to the buyers who said they would never sell?
Did Washington's approval matter at all?
Is this a broken asset, or a changed one?
counter_positions_to_state_fairly: Four-year-cycle believers read this as an ordinary post-halving drawdown, not a structural change
The accumulation data (f-supply-2pct) genuinely cuts against the distribution narrative
Regulatory wins may have long lead times that a 10-month window cannot measure

unknowns.what: RESOLVED (follow-up round 1) — the accumulation and the distribution are different cohorts
unknowns.why: Wallets >1,000 BTC absorbed ~270k BTC; holders of 100-1,000 BTC distributed ~77,800 BTC over the same window, slightly more. Retail distributed too.
unknowns.impact: The script may now STATE the answer instead of hedging between competing readings. Say who the seller is.

unknowns.what: The precise spot price on the day of writing
unknowns.why: Sources in the same week quote $60k, $62k and $65k
unknowns.impact: Say 'around $60,000' or 'roughly half its high'. Never a precise figure.

unknowns.why: Correlation is measured; causation is asserted by analysts

engine_fit.why: The material is literally a chain of four wrong obvious readings, ending in a thesis that reframes the whole subject. r1→r2→r3→r4 is the spine.

The candidate explanations (ETF plumbing / treasury reversal / macro / it's just the cycle) are genuinely competing and can be weighed. Note the D-honest requirement: 'the premise is wrong — it IS rising in some frame' must be in the candidate set.
No news event. This is a standing condition, not something that happened yesterday.
No second domain to transfer to. Gold or equities would be forced.

currency.why: Price levels date immediately; the structural argument (institutionalisation → correlation) has a half-life measured in years
currency.advice: Write the price as a ratio ('roughly half its high') rather than a number, and the script survives months instead of days.

research_gaps: Still no PRIMARY on-chain data — follow-up round 1 improved the cohort picture but every figure remains aggregator-sourced, and several sources wrap them in a bullish framing this notebook does not adopt.
No price series — a chart would settle the price ambiguity and give the Frames step real material.
No bear-case-is-wrong source — did not search for the strongest 'this is normal cycle behaviour' argument, which weakens the steel-man.
Miner economics not researched (post-halving hashprice, capitulation) — a plausible fifth mechanism left unexplored.
